summary: The sitting governor ran again: Phil Scott (Republican) won a sixth two-year term over Amanda Janoo, the Democratic/Progressive nominee.

candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.bio: Phil Scott is the governor of Vermont, in office since 2017. He previously served as lieutenant governor and as a state senator, and co-owned a construction company before selling his share.

positions.summary: Says he opposes new taxes and fees and describes his approach as frugal.
Issued a state order requiring primary care providers and pharmacies to offer COVID-19 vaccines to Vermonters age five and older who want one.
Told the U.S. attorney general that Vermont's sanctuary designation "has been made in error" because the state has no law or policy obstructing federal immigration enforcement.
Proposes consolidating Vermont's 119 school districts into five and giving the state more control over school spending.

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.bio: Amanda Janoo is an economist and a first-time candidate for statewide office. She was the Democratic nominee for Vermont governor in 2026.

positions.summary: Proposes higher income taxes on top earners, including a surcharge on income above $500,000, and higher property taxes on wealthy out-of-state owners.
Proposes a state-funded universal primary care system paid for by taxes on top earners.
Mentioned protecting "small schools" among her priorities in her campaign launch video.
Says she would do "anything I can do legally as governor" to remove the Vermont Air National Guard's F-35 jets from state airspace.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called).
